# LegatorOCR v0.2.0-pre.36 (pre-release)

Changes since pre.35. Written and tried by the author's assistant on one Linux machine. The automated test suite passes on CI runners for Linux x86-64 and arm64, Windows x86-64 and arm64, and macOS (Apple silicon and Intel). **Nothing was tried by hand on Windows, macOS or arm64.**

**New (command line; all are also in the window's "All options")**
- PDF toolbox: `--header`, `--footer`, `--bates PREFIX[:START[:DIGITS]]` (page text and Bates numbers that continue across the files of a run), `--sanitize` (no document information, annotations, page actions, thumbnails), `--rotate-pdf DEG[:RANGES]`, `--crop-pdf L,B,R,T` (mm), `--booklet` (two pages per sheet side in folding order).
- OCR: `--ocr-zone X,Y,W,H[=LANG]` and `--ocr-ignore X,Y,W,H` (read only some areas, in your order, each in its own language, or skip some), `--lang-auto ron,eng,fra` (the language is chosen per page from a list).
- Signing: `--sign-visible PAGE,X,Y,W,H` draws the signature as a box with signer, reason and date.
- Output files: `--encrypt-pdf` with `--pdf-permissions` (AES-256, passwords only from the environment: `LEGATOROCR_PDF_USER_PASSWORD`, `LEGATOROCR_PDF_OWNER_PASSWORD`), `--object-streams` (compressed object streams), `--linearize` (Fast Web View), `--jbig2` (lossless JBIG2 for black & white pages, kept where it is smaller), `--smooth-glyphs 2|3` (smoother glyph edges in black & white output by reading the scan at 2 or 3 times its resolution), `--pdfa-level A|B|U` (PDF/A conformance levels; A turns on the tagged structure and needs `--ocr`).

**Verified**: unit tests for each feature, the full workspace tests, clippy and fmt; the options smoke script; by hand on Linux with qpdf, poppler (`pdftotext`, `pdftoppm`, `pdfinfo`, `pdfsig`): Bates numbers `ACME-0041..0043`, encryption opens with the user password and shows the requested permissions (`qpdf --show-encryption`, `pdfinfo -upw`), `qpdf --check-linearization` finds no errors on 1 to 30 page files, JBIG2 pages render pixel for pixel like the files without it and are 52 % smaller on three noisy synthetic text pages, the visible signature renders as a box and `pdfsig` reads the signature, a six-page booklet gives sides `1 | 2 | 6 3 | 4 5`.
**Not verified**: the booklet printed and folded; OCR zones with Tesseract and the window has no way to draw them; `--lang-auto` on real mixed-language books; opening encrypted, JBIG2 and linearized files in Acrobat or Foxit; veraPDF (not installed): no PDF/A level is validated against the standard; `--smooth-glyphs` is interpolation and cannot restore detail the scan never had (37 % fewer wrong pixels on a test disc); `--object-streams` saves almost nothing on scans (6 KB of 2.8 MB), it pays off on text-only PDFs; the window on Windows, macOS and arm64; the Dockerfile as an image; the translations by native speakers.

**Known limits**: `--encrypt-pdf` is not combined with `--linearize`, `--object-streams` or `--pdfa`; the toolbox still refuses encrypted input; signing needs a classic cross-reference table, so sign before `--object-streams`; `--jbig2` has no symbol dictionaries (no gain from repeated letters); the limits of pre.35 and earlier stand.
